source_caption:
Kedi (2016), directed by Ceyda Torun, is a warm and easygoing documentary set in Istanbul that follows a bunch of stray cats and the people who look after them. It’s less about a big story and more about just spending time in the city, seeing it through these cats as they wander around and quietly become part of people’s lives.

The film keeps things simple and close, often shooting from the cats’ level so you feel like you’re right there with them. You get glimpses of rooftops, busy streets, and quiet corners, all full of life and character. It has a calm, almost relaxing vibe that lets you slow down and take everything in.

At its heart, Kedi is about connection. It shows how even small, everyday interactions can mean a lot, and how humans and animals end up depending on each other in ways we don’t always notice. It’s gentle, a little emotional, and a really nice reminder to appreciate the little things.

source_details.synopsis: Kedi ([keˈdi], Turkish for 'Cat') is a 2016 Turkish documentary film directed by Ceyda Torun about the many stray cats that live in Istanbul. It premiered at the Istanbul Independent Film Festival on 21 February 2016 before being given a North American theatrical release on 10 February 2017. It debuted on the YouTube Red streaming service on 10 May 2017. It was released on DVD in the US on 14 November 2017. The film received critical acclaim, and grossed over $5 million. Time magazine listed it as one of its top ten films of 2017.
